threads.summary: Reopening the database with a different managed merchant\, route contract\, or terms allows existing purchased credit and reservations to execute under that new binding without matching the persisted purchase contract\.
Concurrent imports of the same keyword cohort can overwrite a newer measurement with an older one because the timestamp check runs before SQLite acquires the write transaction\.

P1: This accepts split builds, but the standalone generator embeds only the entry script and blocks external scripts with its CSP; required shared chunks will prevent the preview from starting. Inline the complete module graph or reject builds with required external chunks.

P2: This advertises support for Node 22.0–22.11, but the locked Vite 8.3.5 requires Node 22.12.0 or newer; users on those releases can run the site with an unsupported toolchain. Set the minimum to `>=22.12.0` or retain the previous stricter floor.

P2: The Vercel project settings may be verified, but the production domain binding is still explicitly unverified, and the prerequisite to confirm it was removed. Keep a separate prerequisite to verify that `nexifyai.cloud` is bound to this project before release.

P2: This records the Vercel project as linked and its settings as read back, but `open_prerequisites` still lists `connect_vercel_project`; remove or clarify that stale blocker so operators do not repeat completed setup.
P2: The new checkpoint prose concatenates ordinary words throughout, making deployment and authentication status difficult to parse; restore normal word spacing before merging.
P2: This range admits Node 22.0–22.11, but the locked Vite 8.3.5 dependency requires Node 22.12.0 or newer. Preserve the existing 22.23.4 minimum and cap the range below Node 23.

P2: A clean checkout cannot follow the instruction to read these skills: `.agents/skills/` is gitignored and absent, while `skills-lock.json` contains only hashes. Add a setup step that installs the pinned skills before directing agents to them, or make the instruction conditional on their local availability.

P2: With Clerk enabled, this wrapper loads and initializes `@clerk/react` on every route, including pages that never render an auth panel. Defer the provider until login/signup routes so ordinary public visits avoid the auth SDK cost.
P2: The Clerk sign-in and sign-up widgets stay German when users choose Dutch or French. Select the Clerk localization from the active site locale.
P2: This fallback mounts the full app while Clerk loads, then replaces it with the primary tree, resetting `Workspace` state and potentially losing an in-progress chat. Suspend only the auth widgets.

The relaxed check accepts multi-chunk builds, but the generator still embeds only the entry script, so an entry with a static import of another chunk produces an unusable standalone file. That dependency is neither embedded nor allowed by the standalone content security policy; disabling lazy Clerk initialization does not prevent static imports from loading. Validate that the entry has no external static dependencies, inline its dependency graph, or generate a dedicated single-file offline bundle.

When Clerk is enabled, a failed request for this lazy chunk rejects the import. Suspense only handles loading, and there is no error boundary around the root in main.tsx, so the rejection removes the entire public application instead of showing the unavailable-auth panel. Catch the import failure and keep rendering the public children without auth widgets, or isolate Clerk behind an error boundary with that fallback.

When Clerk is enabled, selecting Nederlands or Français in Workspace changes the surrounding page and account disclaimer, but the sign-in/sign-up forms and validation messages remain German because this provider always receives deDE. Pass the current UI locale into the provider and select the corresponding deDE, nlNL or frFR localization; the new test that explicitly requires deDE should also be updated.

When authentication is enabled, users can create a persistent Clerk session, but neither this panel nor the shared Workspace exposes a sign-out control. On a shared browser, users therefore cannot end their session through the application; `afterSignOutUrl` only configures where an existing sign-out action redirects. Add an accessible signed-in account state with a sign-out control, exposed through the lazy Clerk boundary.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve Vite's minimum Node version**

Setting the package engine to `22.x` declares Node 22.0–22.11 supported, even though the locked Vite 8.3.5 package requires Node `>=22.12.0`. On machines using one of those earlier Node 22 releases, installation may only warn because the application's engine constraint is satisfied, but `pnpm build` or `pnpm dev` can then fail when Vite starts. Retain an explicit lower bound while still excluding Node 23 and later.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Localize Clerk widgets with the selected locale**

When Clerk is enabled and a visitor selects NL or FR, the surrounding authentication page changes language but the Clerk widget remains German because the provider is permanently configured with `deDE` and sits outside the workspace locale context. This produces a mixed-language sign-in/registration flow; pass the selected locale to the provider and choose the corresponding Clerk localization.
